property_summary: When a curated pool calls mintSynth with a positive amount and the pool has newly deposited LP units (>0), the call should not revert (reverted == false).
For any curated pool caller that has increased its LP balance in C (so _getAddedLPAmount>0) and any positive mint amount, mintSynth should not revert (reverted == false).

For any pool caller and any minted amount, calling mintSynth increments mapSynth_LPDebt by exactly the minted amount (debt increase == amount), so mapSynth_LPBalance change is independent of doubling the recorded debt; the mutant that doubles the recorded debt can cause mapSynth_LPBalance for some pool key to differ after an allowance() invocation sequence that leads to minting, violating this invariant.

For any caller and amount, calling allowance(owner, spender) must NOT change any pool's mapSynth_LPBalance; the mutant that doubles recorded debt can make some mapSynth_LPBalance(pool) differ after an allowance-driven sequence (the rule is that allowance calls are view-only and must not mutate mapSynth_LPBalance).

Calling the view function allowance(owner,spender) (and other benign external interactions used in normal ERC20 flows) never changes any pool's mapSynth_LPBalance in the reference contract, but the mutant that doubles recorded debt can cause mapSynth_LPBalance(k) to differ for some pool k after an interaction sequence driven by a pool calling mintSynth, so there exists fuzzed inputs for which mapSynth_LPBalance differs between reference and mutant.

For every inputs, calling allowance(owner,spender) is a view-only call that does not change any mapSynth_LPBalance(key) in the correct contract; the mutant that doubles recorded debt during mintSynth can cause mapSynth_LPBalance(somePool) to differ after allowance-driven interactions, so the invariant is broken for some fuzzed inputs.

After calling mintSynth on a pool, the pool's recorded LP balance for that pool (getmapAddress_LPBalance) increases by exactly the newly added LP units returned by _getAddedLPAmount.
